title: Self-simulation structure
statement: For a function $\Psi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a self-simulation structure consists of a finite Boolean Turing machine $W$ and a decoder assigning a finite Boolean Turing machine to each binary string $\alpha$. For each code $\alpha$, there is a constant $C$ such that whenever the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes a one-bit output $b$ on the paired input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ within $t$ steps, $W$ computes the same output on that input within $C(t+|\langle\alpha,w\rangle|+1)$ steps. Moreover, for every time bound $T$ and every $L \in \mathrm{DTIME}(T)$, there are a code $\alpha$ and a constant $c$ such that, on every input $x$, the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes the indicator of membership in $L$ within $c(\Psi(T(|x|))+1)$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: A decoder from binary strings to finite Boolean Turing machines
For each code $\alpha$, existence of a constant $C$ for the stated self-simulation bound
Existence of a code $\alpha$ and constant $c$ giving the stated bound on every input
